title: ISS measured dose rate, TEPC (NASA SRAG/JSC via CDAWeb)

source.publisher: NASA Space Radiation Analysis Group (JSC), via NASA GSFC Space Physics Data Facility CDAWeb
source.name: ISS_DOSANL_TEPC - Experiment Data, ISS TEPC (from ASCII DOS.TXT file)
source.license: Not stated in the HAPI /info response. The DataCite record of the DOI CDAWeb lists for this dataset (10.48322/0ba1-1764) states Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal (see caveats about that DOI).
source.citation: Semones, E. (contact), NASA Space Radiation Analysis Group / Johnson Space Center. ISS_DOSANL_TEPC: Experiment Data, ISS TEPC (TEPC serial number 1003, analysis software version 3.1), 2010-04-29 to 2018-04-11. NASA GSFC Space Physics Data Facility, CDAWeb HAPI server https://cdaweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/hapi, retrieved 2026-11-14T21:58:12Z. DOI listed by CDAWeb: https://doi.org/10.48322/0ba1-1764 (see caveat on its metadata). https://cdaweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/misc/NotesI.html#ISS_DOSANL_TEPC

caveats: HISTORICAL: the dataset stops at 2018-04-11T23:19:39Z; this is not current ISS dose.

The 24 h native window (2015-06-01) is an arbitrary LANDFALL choice of an ordinary period showing routine SAA modulation; it is not claimed to be typical of other years or of solar-particle-event conditions.

DOSE is absorbed dose (µGy) in the detector; DOSE_EQ60 is the publisher's dose equivalent (ICRP-60 quality factors). Neither is the effective dose (mSv) used by NASA crew exposure limits, so these values must not be compared with those limits directly.

The CDF file also holds LOCATION (where the TEPC was inside the ISS) and FLAG (dominant radiation source); the HAPI server does not expose them, so the detector's location and shielding for this window are unknown here.
Daily dose = sum over the UTC day of DOSE x TIME_INTERVAL; days with < 90 % coverage (design choice) are marked complete=false and excluded from the mean.

CDAWeb lists doi:10.48322/0ba1-1764 for ISS_DOSANL_TEPC, but DataCite's record for that DOI describes 'ISS Tissue-Equivalent Proportional Counter (TEPC), Dose Analyzer, 10 s Data' with coverage 2000-11-09/2010-04-29, while this HAPI dataset spans 2010-2018 at 1 min intervals. The DOI is cited as listed by the publisher; the mismatch is the publisher's metadata, reported here rather than resolved.

data.explainer: What a radiation detector inside the ISS actually measured, minute by minute: a background that rises and falls with latitude on every orbit, and sharp spikes on the orbits that cut through the South Atlantic Anomaly.

dataset.contact: Edward Semones @ NASA Space Radiation Analysis Group/Johnson Space Center

TIME_INTERVAL.description: Number of minutes over which the data was collected

LONGITUDE.description: Geographic longitude of the International Space Station

LATITUDE.description: Geographic latitude of the International Space Station

ALTITUDE.description: Altitude of the International Space Station

native_window.stats_method: Over the non-null native samples, not time-weighted: mean = arithmetic mean, median = middle value (mean of the two middle values for even n), p05/p95 = nearest-rank percentiles (sorted value at rank ceil(q*n)).

daily.method: dose_uGy = sum(DOSE[uGy/min] * TIME_INTERVAL[min]) per UTC day
